title: Enterprise prospect intake — quick-scope card & ROI/compliance filter
creator: Priya Desai
description: Goal: Create a standardized, lightweight Sales/CS intake card and associated quick-scope workflow for enterprise feature requests (non-bug). The card should enable Sales/CS to capture enough information to: 1) decide if a request should proceed to full PM scoping, 2) provide a 1–2 minute ROI/effort heuristic, and 3) surface compliance/regulatory flags early. We want a single-line ask, measurable customer outcome, business justification, high-level technical constraints, and an initial risk/compliance checkbox. This ticket covers template design, recommended auto-populated fields from CRM, a one-click triage rubric (Green / Amber / Red), and a small calculation to estimate monthly ARR uplift vs. rough engineering effort points. Deliverables: intake card template in Zendesk/HubSpot/Salesforce (whichever Sales uses), Confluence doc describing triage rules, a lightweight UI snippet for the CS toolkit, and 2 pilot pockets with Sales and Customer Success for 3 weeks.
acceptance_criteria: A templated intake card exists in the Sales/CS toolchain with required fields (customer name, use-case description, expected ARR impact, compliance flags, target release timeline)
Triage rubric documented in Confluence with clear Green/Amber/Red definitions and example scenarios
A one-click ROI heuristic is implemented (expected ARR uplift / estimated effort points) and validated against 5 historical requests
Pilot with two Sales/CS reps completed and feedback collected (at least 8 sample cards submitted)
Handoff checklist to PM includes required artifacts: product brief, initial risk assessment, and suggested priority
notes: Triage rubric (draft): Green = >$50k ARR potential AND <8 engineering points OR no compliance flags. Amber = $10k–$50k OR 8–20 points OR one compliance item (requires legal review). Red = < $10k and >20 points OR >1 compliance blocker. ROI calc: monthly ARR uplift estimate * 12 / (engineering points * 2) — yields a heuristic score. This is intentionally rough to speed decisions; will iterate after pilot. Link prototype: https://drive.redwood.ai/enterprise-intake/prototype-v1
comments: 2026-03-02 | Priya Desai: Kickoff with Sales Ops — confirmed primary intake will be HubSpot. Sales Ops will add two fields: "Expected ARR (monthly)" and "Strategic Priority". Action: get HubSpot field API schema by 2026-03-06.

2026-03-03 | Asha Kapoor: Initial design pass with Design (Marco Ruiz). We sketched a compact card that places compliance flags next to timeline to increase visibility. Design suggests microcopy for compliance items to reduce legal back-and-forth.

2026-03-04 | Jonah Miller (Eng): Feasibility note — ROI heuristic can be computed in the intake webhook and stored as a custom property. Estimated infra work: 3 dev-days + 1 day testing. Concern: historical data needed for calibration.

2026-03-04 | Legal (Karen Liu): Early compliance review — several enterprise requests may need data residency and encryption answers. We'll add a mandatory checkbox 'requires data residency or export controls' that triggers legal review.

2026-03-05 | Priya Desai: Decision: run two pilots (one from Strategic Sales AM team, one from SMB CS). Pilot duration 3 weeks starting 2026-03-10. Outcome metrics: time-to-triage, accuracy of ROI banding vs. actual scoping, number of legal escalations. Follow-ups: schedule retro 2026-03-31.
review_feedback: Design: favor clear binary compliance flags over free text to reduce misclassification.
Engineering: prefer computing heuristic at intake to avoid manual errors; require minimal fields to avoid friction.
Sales Ops: recommend pre-populating customer ARR from CRM when available to speed submission.
decisions: Use HubSpot as the primary intake surface for Sales; provide a lightweight CS widget for Customer Success.
Implement the ROI heuristic in the intake webhook and store the score as a custom object for reporting.
Add mandatory compliance checkbox that triggers a legal review workflow for Red/Amber items.
